programme: A cell-cycle-exit/AP-1 senescence-effector module: MYBL2 and E2F7 mark durable growth arrest (MYBL2/B-Myb is the MuvB-complex engine of G2/M transcription that is silenced on senescent exit; E2F7 is the atypical repressive E2F induced during that exit, targeting E2F1/E2F2 and CDKN1A), MYC sits at the checkpoint governing whether arrest resolves into senescence versus death, and FOSL1 (Fra-1/AP-1) drives the secretory output of that arrested state through its target MMP1/MMP2/MMP9/MMP13, IL6 and CXCL8. NR4A3 and MEF2D act as amplifiers on the sending and receiving side — NR4A3 as a stress-inducible immediate-early gene shaping monocyte/microglial response to the secreted signal, MEF2D linking the same inflammatory milieu to neuronal apoptotic or lung-epithelial survival decisions — with GFI1 supplying the myeloid-differentiation machinery (SPI1, CSF1R, CSF3, ITGAE) that lets recruited immune cells respond to it.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease this module would correspond to senescent, cell-cycle-arrested glia (and stressed neurons) that stop dividing via the MYBL2/E2F7/MYC checkpoint but remain metabolically active and secretory, releasing FOSL1-driven MMPs and cytokines that remodel matrix around plaques and sustain chronic neuroinflammation, with NR4A3 shaping the microglial/immune response and MEF2D linking that inflammatory state to neuronal apoptotic vulnerability.
role_in_b: In COPD the same checkpoint would mark senescent airway epithelial cells and fibroblasts consistent with the field's 'accelerated lung aging' framing of the disease, with FOSL1-driven MMP1/2/9/13 and IL6/CXCL8 output degrading extracellular matrix (emphysema) and recruiting neutrophils/monocytes, a recruitment GFI1's myeloid programme and NR4A3's monocyte-modulating activity would sustain.
shared_axis: Both diseases are tissue-remote instances of the same generic response — post-mitotic or growth-arrested cells adopting a secretory, matrix-degrading, immune-recruiting phenotype — so the same cell-cycle-exit/AP-1 effector wiring recurs in brain and lung regulatory networks independently, without requiring any organ-to-organ signal.
reasoning: The module is nameable and several of its factors (MYC, NR4A3, FOSL1, MEF2D) each have a retrieved paper placing them in one disease or the other, which is the pattern the record shows for essentially every factor here — none of the retrieved material connects the two diseases directly, so the joining step is domain reasoning about senescence/SASP biology rather than retrieved evidence. Critically, MYBL2 (104/104, the single most recurrent factor) and E2F7 have no usable supporting citation in the record at all, and GFI1's citations are off-target, so the cell-cycle-exit half of the story rests entirely on the factors' known biology, not on what was retrieved.
support: PMID 41038155 (MYC, AD microglial ADGRG1/glial resilience context); PMID 40915373 (MYC, AD mitochondrial energy metabolism via β-catenin/c-Myc/MCT2); PMID 41193654 (MYC, eosinophil-mediated COPD mechanism); PMID 41118410 (MYC, miRNA-regulated inflammatory pathways including COPD); PMID 27159982 (NR4A3, altered NR4A subfamily expression in AD blood); PMID 38474099 (NR4A3, modulates monocyte-linked responses relevant to COPD); PMID 39349220 (FOSL1, implicated in interleukin-associated signaling in an AD neuroprotection study); PMID 41998641 (FOSL1, cited in a COPD neutrophilic-inflammation/PROK2 study, relevance to FOSL1 itself uncertain); PMID 19801631 (MEF2D, GSK3β-driven neuronal apoptosis in AD); PMID 28340574 (MEF2D, crosstalk between chronic inflammation and lung cancer/respiratory disease). MYBL2, E2F7 and GFI1: none found that support their role in either disease (MYBL2's only hit, PMID 32264724, is an unrelated autophagy review explicitly noted as not confirming involvement).
how_to_falsify: Stain AD hippocampal tissue and COPD lung tissue for canonical senescence markers (p16/p21, SA-β-gal) and test by co-IF or ChIP whether senescent cells in both tissues show DREAM/MuvB-mediated repression of MYBL2 and E2F7 target genes together with FOSL1-driven transcription of MMP1/2/9/13, IL6 and CXCL8; if senescent cells in either tissue lack that specific pairing (arrest signature without the AP-1 secretory signature, or vice versa), the proposed shared module does not hold. A complementary test: FOSL1 knockdown in senescent brain organoid glia and senescent bronchial epithelial cells should suppress the same MMP/IL6/CXCL8 output in both if the mechanism is truly shared.
caveats: Brain and lung do not communicate directly, so any shared signal must run through this kind of tissue-independent cellular programme rather than organ crosstalk — the account is only as strong as that assumption. Support is drawn from 104 patient-group comparisons across just 6 independent cohort pairs, so the recurrence counts, while high for MYBL2 (104/104) and NR4A3 (96/104), reflect a small number of underlying independent samples. The tissue-generic exclusion list (SOX10, ZEB1, NOTCH1, NR3C1, etc.) rules out the tempting 'master regulator of neural or lung tissue' story — none of those appear here, which is a feature of the account, not a gap. Five factors in the surviving list (HOXA13, HOXA11, AR, KDM5B, ELK3) were left out of the programme because they read as developmental/vascular/chromatin factors with no clear fit to a senescence-SASP axis and, per the record, have thin or absent literature support in either disease — their recurrence is real but this account cannot explain them, which should be treated as an open gap rather than folded in.
